2 (pedestrian)details:on [date] i, sgt. layland with the joshua isd police department was located in the [roadway]. joshua, texas 76058. at approximately 08:07:20 (unit 2 pedestrian) was observed to begin running from 909 s. broadway joshua, tx. 76058 ([school facility]) towards the roadway. an employee / [school facility] district was at the time located in the roadway directing traffic in the crosswalk located in approximately the [roadway]. joshua, texas 76058. sgt. layland heard the witness yell at the student to stop as traffic was open for movement and closed to pedestrians at the time. sgt. layland observed unit 2 (pedestrian) enter the roadway against the direction of the district employee and attempt to cut between traffic. unit 2 ran in front of a white in color sedan before striking the drivers side of a 2023 chevrolet [roadway] causing damages. the vehicle blue in color was operated by unit 1 driver. sgt. layland immediately made contact with unit 2 (pedestrian) who advised he was in a hurry for class and didn't want to wait for traffic to be stopped for pedestrians to cross. unit 2 indicated he did not see unit 1 until he hit it. unit 2 (pedestrian) declined medical [school facility] where he was initially seen by the nurse out of an abundance of caution. sgt. layland relocated back to make contact with unit 1. unit 1 who had relocated out of the roadway was parked on campus grounds awaiting contact. sgt. layland observed the vehicle to sustain front driver side damage to the fender, door and mirror, as well as a scratch was observed on the driver side of the bed. sgt. layland collected driver, and vehicle information. photos were taken for documentational purposes. careflite ops 2 arrived on scene. ems checked out unit 2 (pedestrian) as a precautionary measure. careflite cleared scene. nothing further to report at this time.

records.deidentified_narrative: the listed location is a private parking lot for a clinic. unit 2, a pedestrian, was crossing the parking lot from the office side toward the vehicle travel portion. unit 2 had nearly crossed when she was struck by unit 1, a motor vehicle. i made contact with the driver of unit 1. he stated that he had pulled around and was preparing to exit the [roadway]. he advised he was traveling at a slow speed due to limited visibility caused by sun glare from the east and tree sap on the vehicle's windshield, which further impaired his line of sight. the driver stated he did not see the pedestrian and only became aware of her presence after hearing a thumping sound. he immediately stopped the vehicle and then observed unit 2 on the ground. under texas transportation code § 552. 006, a driver operating a vehicle on a roadway (including a private parking area open to vehicular traffic) shall yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian crossing the roadway in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. drivers are also required under § 545. 401 to exercise due care to avoid colliding with a pedestrian. based on the driver's statement and the position of the pedestrian, it appears that unit 1 failed to exercise due care by operating a vehicle with impaired visibility and did not yield to a pedestrian. tid was notified of the crash and advised that there were no life threatening injuries and unit 1 remained on scene.
